subject: RFP: Throughput acceptance criteria and scaling scenarios
messages:
From: Ryan Cole <ops@edgebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@edgebank.com>, Benchmark Labs <benchmarks@benchmarklabs.io>
Date: 2026-09-25T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — initial ask

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the earlier packet — Procurement asked us to clarify the performance evidence we need for the RFP. Specifically, we need a concise acceptance matrix showing throughput (TPS/QPS), p50/p95/p99 latencies, and resource footprint for the following representative workloads:

- Interactive chat (avg seq len 64, 8 tokens/sec sustained per session)
- Batch embeddings (avg 1024 tokens, 500 concurrent jobs)
- Mixed fanout inference (calling multiple models for reranking pipeline; median fanout 3)

For each workload we want:
1) Test method description (load generator, traffic shaping, artifact capture).
2) Environment used (instance type/GPU, model name + quantization, batch config).
3) Raw metrics (throughput, token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency in ms) and profiling notes (KV cache hit rates, batching efficiency).
4) Failure modes observed during previous runs and recommended graceful-degradation configs.

Can you provide an acceptance matrix (spreadsheet) plus a short runbook we can hand to our benchmarking partner (Benchmark Labs) so they can reproduce? Timeline: procurement needs deliverables by EOD 2026-09-29.

Appreciate it — if a call helps, ping procurement for a 30-min slot.

Ryan Cole
Senior Ops Lead, EdgeBank
ops@edgebank.com
[Attachment: edgebank-rfp-exec-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ryan Cole <ops@edgebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — initial ask

Ryan — thanks for the clarity. We're able to produce the matrix and a reproducible runbook. High level approach:

- We will supply a CSV acceptance matrix mapping workload -> test case IDs -> target SLOs.
- Provide a self-contained test harness spec (traffic generator command lines, seed traces for session interleaving, input distributions).
- Include environment sheet listing model versions (e.g., t5-large-quantized-INT8), GPU/driver/kernel combos we used, and notes on kernel selection.

Two clarifications before we finalize:
1) For the interactive chat workload do you want end-to-end user-to-response latency (includes network and client-side batching) or backend-only server processing time? Our standard RFP deliverable is backend processing time (server-side) but we can annotate an estimated e2e add-on.
2) For the mixed fanout pipeline should we include a worst-case fallback scenario (one model slow / one model OOM) and show graceful degradation sequencing (e.g., fall back to lower-precision variant)?

Ben/Marissa — can one of you attach the CSV template and the env-spec workbook? Grace — can you draft the short runbook (1–2 pages) with exact commands for Benchmark Labs to run?

I'll assemble and submit by EOD 2026-09-29 as requested. If procurement needs an earlier review, happy to do a short walkthrough tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-rfp-guidelines.txt (text/plain)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — CSV template and env specs

Attaching the requested artifacts. Notes embedded in the CSV: test-case IDs 100–199 cover interactive chat slices, 200–299 cover embeddings, 300–399 cover mixed fanout. Key columns: workload_id, seq_len_distribution, target_qps, measured_p50_ms, measured_p95_ms, measured_p99_ms, gpu_type, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_policy, notes.

Quick callouts from recent internal runs (relevant to EdgeBank):
- On A100-80GB with INT8 quantized LLM, interactive chat avg seq len 64, we sustain 450 qps at p95 ~ 85ms backend processing (p99 ~ 170ms) when using continuous batching with a 50ms batching window.
- Embeddings workload (batching 256 inputs) reached 12k embeddings/sec on a 4xA10 pod (aggregate), with p99 dominated by disk I/O on the job queue when using shared NFS for inputs — recommend S3 stream ingestion for large batches.
- Mixed fanout: graceful degradation tested by substituting a 7B family fallback for the primary 13B model; end-to-end callback latency increased predictably but preserved throughput for the primary route.

Attachments: redwood-throughput-matrix-v1.csv, env-specs-gpu-and-kernel-table.xlsx.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-throughput-matrix-v1.csv (text/csv), env-specs-gpu-and-kernel-table.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Benchmark Labs <benchmarks@benchmarklabs.io>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — runbook and reproducibility notes

Hi team (and Benchmark Labs),

Attached is the 2-page runbook with exact steps to reproduce our test cases. Highlights:
- All tests use our open-source harness (redwood-loadgen v0.9) with provided seed traces. Example command: 
  redwood-loadgen --case-id 101 --concurrency 120 --seq-dist seq64.json --batch-window-ms 50 --reporting p50,p95,p99 --out artifacts/101
- For model runtime we specify driver/kernel combos; if you cannot match the exact kernel, capture the kernel name and we will map expected delta in performance.
- KV cache warmup protocol: run 100 warmup sessions per endpoint to reach steady-state cache hit rates.
- Failure-mode experiments: include an induced OOM on the secondary model to verify fallback path and measure increase in p95/p99.

Please run case IDs 110, 215, and 312 as representative checks and push the raw CSVs back to the Drive folder in the related links. We will review the output and sign-off if metrics meet the acceptance matrix targets.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Performance PM — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: test-harness-instructions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ryan Cole <ops@edgebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Benchmark Labs <benchmarks@benchmarklabs.io>, Procurement <procurement@edgebank.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — deliverables received

Irene/Grace/Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. We received the CSV matrix and the runbook, and Benchmark Labs confirmed they can reproduce cases 110/215/312 this morning. A couple of small follow-ups:

- For the CSV row notes, can you expand the kv_cache_policy column to indicate expected warmup time to 95% hit rate (minutes)? That helps our ops schedule warmup windows in production.
- For the A100 measurements, please include the driver and CUDA versions used so we can ensure parity in our cloud tenancy.
- Procurement asked for an explicit statement of whether the p99 numbers are measured over a 5-minute steady-state window or the full test duration.

If you can add those three clarifications as an annotated CSV and a one-paragraph addendum, procurement will accept the evidence package. Can you deliver by EOD today?

Best,
Ryan
Senior Ops Lead, EdgeBank
ops@edgebank.com

On Sep 29, 2026, 09:25 AM, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — we'll add the warmup minutes column, driver/CUDA versions, and the p99 measurement note (we use a 5-minute steady-state window by default, will annotate). Ben/Grace: can one of you update and push before 17:00 PDT?
>
> Irene
> Director, Product — Redwood Inference
